patches.title: [PATCH v3 1/2] PCI: plda: Fix use-after-free of event IRQs during teardown
patches.description: Fixed a use-after-free in the shared PLDA PCIe host teardown path. plda_pcie_irq_domain_deinit() removed the event IRQ domain with irq_domain_remove(), but the per-event IRQs mapped from that domain are requested with devm_request_irq(), so their free_irq() is deferred by devres until after remove() returns and could dereference the already-freed domain. Each event IRQ is now released explicitly with devm_free_irq() before the domain goes away, the event, INTx, and MSI mappings are disposed of with irq_dispose_mapping(), and the chained-handler teardown is guarded so it only runs for valid IRQ numbers.
patches.impact: Removes a use-after-free that could be triggered on driver unbind or module unload on every PLDA-based controller, including StarFive JH7110 and Microchip PolarFire. Also makes teardown safe when it runs from a partially initialized state, and stops IRQ mappings from being leaked. Tagged for stable backport.
patches.testing: Build-tested and boot-tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A.

patches.title: PCI: plda: Fix IRQ domain leaks in the error paths of plda_init_interrupts()
patches.description: plda_init_interrupts() created IRQ domains and IRQ mappings but never unwound them when a later step failed, so a failing platform_get_irq() or irq_create_mapping() left the domains allocated and port->intx_irq still initialized. The error paths now call plda_pcie_irq_domain_deinit(), which also disposes of the INTx and MSI mappings itself, so the MSI failure path can unwind through a single label.
patches.impact: Prevents permanently leaked IRQ domains and IRQ descriptors when PCIe interrupt setup fails during probe, which previously left kernel resources stranded even after the driver bailed out. Tagged for stable backport.

patches.title: [PATCH v3] PCI: starfive: Fix resource leaks on error paths in host_init()
patches.description: Fixed resource leaks in the StarFive JH7110 PCIe host initialization path. The driver could leave the PHY and clock/reset resources enabled when later setup steps failed, leaving the controller in an inconsistent state and leaking resources. The fix now tears down these resources correctly on error paths and returns the failure status properly.
patches.impact: Prevents leaked PHY, clock, and reset resources during PCIe probe failures and ensures the driver leaves the hardware in a consistent state when initialization aborts. This improves robustness and reliability of PCIe bring-up on StarFive platforms.
patches.testing: Built and boot-tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A. Verified that error-path cleanup works correctly during failed initialization.

patches.title: [PATCH v2] PCI: starfive: Fix Runtime PM handling and teardown ordering
patches.description: starfive_pcie_remove() dropped the runtime PM reference and disabled runtime PM before calling plda_pcie_host_deinit(), so host teardown could reach controller registers after the power domain and clocks were already gone. Removal now deinitializes the host first, while runtime PM is still active, and only then calls pm_runtime_put_sync() and pm_runtime_disable(). The asynchronous pm_runtime_put() was also swapped for the synchronous variant, since the immediately following pm_runtime_disable() would otherwise cancel the queued idle request and leave the device stuck in an active power state.
patches.impact: Prevents unclocked register access during driver unbind or module unload, which can fault on RISC-V hardware, and ensures the PCIe controller actually powers down on removal instead of being left permanently active.

patches.title: [PATCH v2] PCI: starfive: Fix unchecked pm_runtime_get_sync() in probe
patches.description: starfive_pcie_probe() called pm_runtime_get_sync() without checking its return value, so a failed runtime resume still let the driver go on to program PCIe registers through regmap_update_bits(), enable clocks and resets, and power on the PHY on a device that may not have been powered. pm_runtime_get_sync() also leaves the usage counter incremented when resume fails. The probe now uses pm_runtime_resume_and_get(), which balances the counter internally, and bails out before any hardware is touched.
patches.impact: Stops PCIe bring-up from proceeding on an unpowered controller, where register access can hang or fault the CPU, and keeps the runtime PM usage count balanced so later suspend and resume cycles track the real power state.
patches.testing: Tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A board.

patches.title: [PATCH] rtl8xxxu: fix slab-out-of-bounds in rtl8xxxu_sta_add
patches.description: Fixed a critical memory safety issue in the rtl8xxxu wireless driver. The driver wasn't setting hw->sta_data_size, causing mac80211 to allocate insufficient space for per-station private data. This resulted in slab-out-of-bounds writes when rtl8xxxu_sta_add() accessed sta->drv_priv members. Bug was caught by KASAN on RISC-V hardware with RTL8192EU adapter.
patches.impact: Fixes memory corruption vulnerability that could cause kernel crashes, data corruption, or potential security issues. Prevents KASAN-detected slab-out-of-bounds write in station addition path. This is a critical correctness fix that ensures proper memory allocation for driver private data structures in mac80211 wireless stack. Also tagged for stable kernel backport.
patches.testing: Tested with RTL8192EU adapter on StarFive VisionFive 2 (RISC-V). Verified with KASAN enabled that the slab-out-of-bounds write is eliminated.

patches.title: [PATCH] spi: cadence-qspi: Fix runtime PM imbalance in probe
patches.description: Fixed a runtime PM reference count underflow in the Cadence Quad SPI controller driver. The probe function was incorrectly calling pm_runtime_put_autosuspend() twice while only acquiring one reference with pm_runtime_get_sync(), causing usage count to go negative.
patches.impact: Prevents runtime PM subsystem corruption and fixes kernel warning "Runtime PM usage count underflow!" on affected hardware. Ensures correct power management state tracking for SPI controller, preventing potential power management issues during device suspend/resume cycles.
patches.testing: Verified on StarFive VisionFive 2 that the runtime PM warning no longer appears during boot and driver probe.

patches.title: [PATCH v3] pinctrl: starfive: use dynamic GPIO base allocation
patches.description: Modernized the StarFive JH7110 (RISC-V SoC) pinctrl driver to use dynamic GPIO base allocation instead of deprecated static assignment. Removed hardcoded gc_base values and associated constants (JH7110_SYS_GC_BASE, JH7110_AON_GC_BASE) that are no longer needed with dynamic allocation.
patches.impact: Eliminates kernel deprecation warning "Static allocation of GPIO base is deprecated, use dynamic allocation." Aligns driver with current GPIO subsystem best practices and prevents potential GPIO numbering conflicts in complex systems. Makes the driver more maintainable and future-proof as the GPIO subsystem moves away from static base assignment.
patches.testing: Tested on StarFive VisionFive 2. Verified GPIO functionality remains correct with dynamic allocation. Confirmed no deprecation warnings during boot.
